# SO-101 robot description

Vendored so the simulation does not depend on a checkout belonging to another
project. Copied byte-identical from
`/home/wangyun/intern/RLT_dual/third_party/SO101` on 2026-08-14.

Upstream origin: the `so101_new_calib` description from LeRobot / TheRobotStudio
SO-ARM100, generated by `onshape-to-robot` (see the header comment in the URDF
for the CAD document link).

## Contents

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `so101_new_calib.urdf` | 6-DoF follower arm, the one the simulator builds from |
| `so101_new_calib_fk.urdf` | forward-kinematics variant, unused by the sim |
| `assets/*.stl` | 13 meshes, ~16 MB, used for both visual and collision geometry |

## Why this one and not SO-ARM100

`mujoco_menagerie/trs_so_arm100` is the **SO-ARM100**, a different arm. This is
the SO-101, and its six joint names match LeRobot's motor table exactly --
`shoulder_pan`, `shoulder_lift`, `elbow_flex`, `wrist_flex`, `wrist_roll`,
`gripper`, in that order -- so `{motor}.pos` keys need no remapping.

## What the build does to it

`src/evo_rlt/sim/assets.py` never modifies these files. It writes a patched copy
into the asset cache with a `<mujoco><compiler>` tag added, because MuJoCo's URDF
reader needs `meshdir="assets"` and `discardvisual="false"` (its default of
`true` would throw away the visual meshes and leave the cameras rendering
collision geometry).

Joint limits here are the source of `URDF_JOINT_LIMITS` in
`src/evo_rlt/sim/calib.py`. If this URDF is ever replaced, those constants must
be re-derived.
